header.title: Level 2: working an inventory
header.briefing: Five client requests in a row. Price each one (or pass), then hedge or keep the risk before the market moves. Your inventory and P&L carry from one request to the next.

risk_card.title: Training assumptions (a simplified model for this exercise, not estimates of true market volatility)

conditions.flow: one-way: about 70% of this morning's inquiries were clients who pay fixed.
conditions.desk_expectation: if that continues, the next few inquiries lean towards clients who pay fixed.

observation.prompt: Your rate for the client to pay at (or 'pass')?

reasons: Risk-adding trade with your limit getting full: pricing it wide is the right instinct.

input.hint: 'none'; '50%' (of your DV01, in the 5Y); '100% 5y'; 'pay 150m 10y'; or two legs: 'pay 150m 10y + receive 60m 30y'

reasons: A reasonable trade-off for a reasonable risk appetite. For a middle-of-the-range appetite the best balance is: hedge 100% in the 5y.
Your choice: cost now €6,123, risk over the next step sigma €39,024 (keeping the book as it is: sigma €151,525).
You are left with a curve position: +30,613 EUR per bp of slope beyond your outright risk. A DV01 hedge in another tenor hedges the level, not the curve.
